sets.label: 2026-09-05 · D + free: the free-set / peaks-only / class-C variants of the D-id100-negrich recipe (proposal, no default flipped)
sets.note: FOUR coordinate slices (156 / +72 peaks / +109 free / +133 free+classC) x THREE dial variants (base / -id100 clamped anchor / -id100-negrich unclamped + identity x21), all on ONE leg (r1b-pools944 safesyn, 111k) at lambda=0.3 — so a difference between rows of one variant is the SLICE and a difference down a slice's three rows is the DIAL. Rank is identical across a slice's three variants to <=1e-4 (monotone remap), so read rank ACROSS and dial DOWN. Every -id100-negrich arm is CONTRACT 6/6 + REGRESSION 7/9 against the ssim2 bars on this era's own 944-POOLS instruments (grid 694e16c4, negtail bafc8994, identity 31fc4403 — registered 2026-09-05, NOT the 372 bars; A8 in particular is a far easier bar on this probe, -64.23 vs -187.13). The clamped -id100 arms fix C5 and break C3/C4, re-deriving the D lane's 'the lever is the clamp, not the anchor'. HEADLINE: the ZERO-marginal-compute half of the free set carries it — Fpeaks gets 97% of the CID22 gain, 95% of KonJND, 99.5% of hfnlproxy and 96%/98% of the hfnl_cid22band pooled/per-ref gain, and BEATS the full free set on 8 of 12 corpora. NOT COMPARABLE to D-id100-negrich's published numbers: different training leg, measured here at -0.056 CID22 on the matched 156-only control. Record: benchmarks/d_free_id100_2026-09-05.md.

sets.label: 2026-09-04 · B dial re-anchor: imazen-26 vs safesyn, ERA vs CONTENT (proposal, no default flipped)
sets.note: Four dial arms over IDENTICAL weights/scaler/winsor — only the output spline differs, so SROCC is identical to 5 dp on all five corpora by construction; read the DIAL columns, not the rank ones. oldanchor_full = the procedure floor (+0.031 CID22 vs shipped, and sha 62d8274c reproduces the b_reextract lane's armN independently). safesyn_curera = the SAME 2,000 shipped-anchor rows re-decoded + re-extracted 2026-09-04 with targets unchanged, so (curera - oldanchor_full) is the ERA term with content EXACTLY fixed: +3.892 CID22 / +4.798 KonJND / +3.864 AIC-3. im26anchor swaps content on top, adding only -0.395 / -0.989 / -0.233 — era is 4-10x content, which overturns b_reextract §9d's confounded +-6-8pt content estimate. im26top is the extend-top-anchor-swap-only arm and moves the human corpora by 0.000 BY DESIGN (extend-top keeps in-distribution knots verbatim; CID22 tops out at 90.41, below the extension domain). NOT A SHIP CANDIDATE: im26anchor's dial reach falls 96.85 -> 85.74. im26_topdense is the reach-preserving anchor variant (reach 85.74 -> 88.96, p95 98.44 -> 99.12, but p5 unmoved -- the floor is shared-anchor's, not extend-top's). The FOUR arms above all share identical WEIGHTS, so their rank rows are identical by construction. The last three do NOT: konctl/konim26/konim26_anchim26 re-fit B's kon head with safesyn replaced by a mass-matched imazen-26 leg, and that is a MEASURED NEGATIVE -- CID22 0.88212 -> 0.85100 and AIC-3 -0.00321 (both genuine holdouts DOWN) while TID +0.0157 and KADID +0.0179 (both kon-head training corpora) go up; M3a 0.6023 -> 0.5683 and product_composite 0.8286 -> 0.8214. konctl is byte-identical to the b_reextract lane's armC (f08b3c80). Mass-matching is not diversity-matching: safesyn spans 1,495 refs and six codec families, the imazen-26 leg 212 origins and four. Record: benchmarks/imazen26_anchor_2026-09-04.md.

sets.label: 2026-09-01 · wave-r4 era-2×radius-4 retrain — nothing passes W1–W7 (14 arms promoted)
sets.note: wave_r4_2026-09-01.md §19 closing exam: NOTHING in this wave passes W1–W7 against peer_ssim2, matching the exam's own pre-registered expectation. 16 fullevals existed on disk; 14 promoted here (A4b_s4004 already on the board, sha256-identical, promoted earlier this session as K4 in the a4bkon lane -- not re-promoted; A1_r4_s4004 SKIPPED -- it is the pre-fix wrong-regime diagnostic run §7.3/§7.6 explicitly says is 'not cited' (best_val 0.3058, dial-mono 0.9271 below the 0.93 gate, silently fell back to the era-1 features root) and is kept on disk only as regime-mismatch evidence, not a candidate arm; the doc's real A1 flagship citation is A1foldapp2_r4_s4004/s4005, both promoted). Two honest rankings: A5 s4005 (944, kon w=2.4) is the cleanest W1 profile in the whole wave (its only miss is the same raw-delta KonJND edge every 944-class arm shows, Δ−0.0195, CID22 flat); A4b (156+free, distill target, teacher HYA_w084) is the cleanest in the 156-class-ish family, matching A1foldapp2's own single-axis KonJND-only failure shape at roughly a fifth of the 944-class extraction cost, and posts the highest product composite of any arm scored this wave (0.8664, beating the 944 teacher's own 0.8601). A6 (196k safesyn leg, §21) is the wave's biggest single lever: +0.0617 CID22 over its 111k control (A2) at λ=0.002 and +0.023 at λ=0.3, cross-checking the hybrid lane's independent +0.057 citation within 0.005. The free-set (156+free) family wins on every axis over its 156-only control at zero extra training-data cost: A2b vs A2ctrl at matched λ=0.3, CID22 +0.031, KonJND +0.071, CSIQ +0.025, hfnl_cid22band +0.05 pooled (§14.2) -- though both still fail W6's 0.85 nonphoto floor, the one axis where architecture class (additive vs MLP) decides regardless of slice width. W4: every 944-class arm (A1foldapp2, A5) fails structurally at both 1T and 8T (worse threaded, 2.1–4.1x over the 1.25x bar); every 156-class arm (A2/A2ctrl/A3/A4/A6) passes by architecture-class construction; the two free-set MLPs (A3b/A4b) pass evidence-backed (~5–7% over the add156_156basic walk, not a direct bench-measured arm) rather than automatically. W7 (default-build reachability) fails for every arm in this wave -- none is wired into a ZensimProfile variant; that remains a follow-up product decision, out of scope here. Two data-integrity bugs this wave found and fixed in-flight, both flagged in §7: the wave root's regime didn't match the flagship recipe's training regime (foldapp2pools vs foldapp2, §7.3), and kadid_pairs_ab.tsv still carries the pre-2026-08-05 INVERTED KADID target so any fresh extraction re-introduces the bug until the TSV itself is fixed at its owner (§7.4).

sets.label: 2026-09-04 · D-id100: Profile D with the identity pinned at 100 (proposal, no default flipped)
sets.note: Three cells over BYTE-IDENTICAL weights — stripping the spline and the repro block from all three yields sha256 330d8c09…, the shipped Profile D fit. Only the output-calibration spline differs, so every rank column is the same number by construction (paired bootstrap ΔSROCC 95% CI = [0,0] on cid22/konjnd/aic3/csiq/nonphoto/imazen26; ≤8e-6 on tid/live/kadid, and ZERO pair-order flips on all 14 corpora — the residue is tie structure). READ THE DIAL COLUMNS. D_shipped_ctl is the byte-exact reproduction of the shipped d_sdr_add156_dense_dial bake (sha 4481c2d4…), included as the era-matched reference read in the same run. d_id100 adds 21 identity rows (feature 0⃗ ↦ 100) to the spline anchor; d_id100_negrich additionally reads the anchor's OWN unclamped ssim2_gpu column instead of target_score = max(ssim2,0). G-ADDR (peer_ssim2 bars): shipped D CONTRACT 5/6 + REGRESSION 2/9 → d_id100 6/6 + 4/9 → d_id100_negrich 6/6 + 7/9. Record: benchmarks/d_id100_2026-09-04.md.

sets.label: 2026-09-05 · replication wave: ORDER-vs-INIT arms on the corrected top recipes (LSTAR / LSTAR3 / W11J) + their diagonals
sets.note: Arm S = sample/ORDER varies at fixed init; arm I = init varies at fixed order; the legacy --seed draws on the board are the confounded DIAGONAL and belong to both arms. CTL_A/CTL_B are the equivalence controls (legacy --seed 4021 vs --init-seed 4021 --sample-seed 4021): 0 of 12 corpora differ and the composite matches to 16 digits, which is why the diagonal may be pooled. READ A GROUP DOWN — k-mean and spread, never best-of-k; best-of-k inflates the composite by a median +0.0061 on this board. These three recipes only became visible AS recipes after the 2026-09-05 grouping fixes (--dump-checkpoints-dir and argv[0] were part of the recipe key, so every seed looked like its own k=1 recipe). A3b — the one genuinely-k=1 fair-board recipe — is not in THIS set because it is era-2 x radius-4 and must be scored at its native root; that is no longer a blocker (run_full_eval.sh now takes the features root FROM THE BAKE, 2026-09-05) and its four cells are the 2026-09-05-a3b-native set. Read them DOWN, never against a canonical-root cell — different feature space. Its arm is in benchmarks/replication_wave_2026-09-05.md.

sets.label: 2026-09-05 · A3b at its NATIVE root (era-2×radius-4): the four cells run_full_eval.sh could not produce before the features root came from the bake
sets.note: A3b is the replication wave's one genuinely-k=1 recipe and it had NO complete board cell: bake_verdict correctly REFUSES it at the canonical folded root (it structurally uses 72 caller lines in f156-371, which that root feeds as structural zeros), and run_full_eval.sh hard-coded one features root per regime, so no fulleval — and therefore no M3a, and therefore no selectable cell — could be produced (replication_wave_2026-09-05.md §4c.3). The features root now comes FROM THE BAKE (zensim_validate::feature_set::resolve_features_root, via `bake_verdict --print-features-root`), so all four cells are read on /mnt/v/zen/zensim-training/ext944-era2r4-2026-09-01 and carry M3a. READ DOWN, NOT ACROSS: that root is a DIFFERENT feature space from the --regime 944 default, so an A3b number is not comparable with a canonical-root number. A3b_s4004 and A3b__D__i4004_p4004_packed are the same recipe on the same seeds (i4004/p4004) packed twice — identical CID22 to 16 digits, composite differing at the 9th decimal, but M3a 0.7489 vs 0.8618: attribution density is sensitive to the pack, and the two bakes have different sha256.

sets.label: 2026-09-05 · the D ship flip: what became the shipped dial, what it replaced, and the 944 arm that could not ship
sets.note: USER DECISION 2026-09-05: `ZensimProfile::D`'s default bake is now `d_sdr_add156_id100_negrich_dial_2026-09-05.bin` = the cell **d_id100_negrich@did100lane** (sha256 921a8f67...). It REPLACES **D_shipped_ctl@did100lane** (sha256 4481c2d4...), whose name now means the ERA-1 dial rather than 'the shipped D' — read that cell as the predecessor. The two share BYTE-IDENTICAL weights (both strip to 330d8c09...), so read their RANK columns as one number: bit-identical on 11 of 14 corpora, and kadid/live/tid differ by -1.27e-7/+5.81e-7/+7.93e-6, the tie residue of a monotone remap. Everything that separates them is DIAL: CONTRACT 5/6 -> 6/6, REGRESSION 2/9 -> 7/9, identity 96.1157 -> 100.0000, reach 108.25 -> 156.55, negtail floor -100.0 -> -213.1, 0 of 4,424 cells above identity in BOTH. d_id100@did100lane is the identity pin alone (4/9) and is the smaller move that was not taken. **Fpeaks_id100negrich@dfreelane is the arm the user's words named and it did NOT ship** - it is 944-declared-width, and installing it makes `Zensim::compute()` return ModelForwardFailed on every non-identical pair (MEASURED by doing it), the same limitation profile_c_tests::compute_on_non_identical_pair_fails_loud already pins for C; and its CID22 on its own native root is 0.8465 against shipped D's 0.8634. DO NOT RANK ACROSS THE TWO LANES: the @dfreelane cells are read on the 944-POOLS instruments and the 111k pools-944 leg, the @did100lane cells on the 372 root and ADD156's own 196k leg. Record: benchmarks/d_ship_flip_2026-09-05.md.
